fallacies.name: Ad hominem
fallacies.plain: Going after the person instead of what they said, so their point seems not to count. Like "you can't talk about saving money, you bought a new phone last month."

fallacies.name: Appeal to popularity
fallacies.plain: Saying something must be true or good because lots of people believe it or do it. Like "everyone's buying these shoes, so they must be the best."

fallacies.name: Cherry-picking
fallacies.plain: Showing only the facts that help your side and leaving out the ones that don't. Like an ad quoting the one good review and skipping the twenty bad ones.

fallacies.name: False dilemma
fallacies.plain: Acting like there are only two choices when there are more. Like "either you're with us or you're against us."

fallacies.name: Proof surrogate
fallacies.plain: Using confidence, big words or "trust me" in place of actual evidence. Like "studies show it works, trust me", with no study named.

fallacies.name: Regression fallacy
fallacies.plain: Thinking something worked when things only went back to normal after an unusually good or bad time. Like a new coach getting the credit when the team has a normal season after its worst one.

fallacies.name: Slippery-slope fallacy
fallacies.plain: Saying one small step will lead to something extreme, without showing how. Like "if you stay up late tonight, soon you'll never sleep and you'll fail school."

fallacies.name: Straw man
fallacies.plain: Changing what someone said into something more extreme or silly, then arguing with that instead. Like replying to "I'd like fewer sweets in the house" with "so you want to ban dessert forever?"
